question: The range of electrostatic voltmeter can be extended with the help of:
solution:
The correct answer is __Resistance Potential Divider**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistance Potential Divider__ is used to extend the range of an electrostatic voltmeter.
 
• It divides the voltage into smaller parts, allowing measurement of higher voltages without damaging the voltmeter.
 
• It is constructed using high-value resistances to ensure minimal current flow through the circuit.
 
• The potential divider principle is based on Ohm's Law, ensuring accurate voltage division.
 
• Resistance potential dividers are widely used in high-voltage applications for safe measurements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Capacitance Potential Divider:**
 
 
• This works based on the principle of dividing voltage using capacitors connected in series.
 
• It is used in applications where high-frequency signals need to be measured.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are electronic storage devices that hold data temporarily in digital systems.
 
• They cannot extend the range of an electrostatic voltmeter.
 
 
 
• **Capacitors:**
 
 
• Capacitors store electrical energy but are not used directly for range extension in voltmeters.
